courier.$comment: Street-courier (livreur) flipbook. OUTCOME after the art gates: the RIDER layer is the shipped sprite — a complete cyclist (FLUX base, frame 1) whose 6 frames get rotating wheel spokes stamped by scripts/retouch-courier-spokes.mjs; the BIKE layer passed its gate but was retired from the composite (art kept as spare, its mesh only serves the pre-art fallback) — see src/render/scene/CourierSprite.tsx. Single source of truth for scripts/gen-courier-sprites.mjs. PER-FRAME GENERATION (ADR 0017, amended — the strip-and-slice strategy was retired after two CI iterations cut subjects across cells): each frames[i] is a NON-EMPTY pose clause and becomes ONE dedicated FLUX image (opening + prompt + clause + style) under the layer's single pinned seed, so the whole subject appears in every image and only the described delta moves. Each PNG is chroma-keyed per file (cutout-enemies.mjs cutout()). No protected committed frame 1 — if ANY frame file of a layer is missing (or FORCE=1), ALL its frames regenerate together (shared-seed consistency makes the layer atomic). Files: public/assets/courier/<layer>.png + <layer>_f<N>.png (frame 1 unsuffixed). scale/offsetY are render-side registration knobs tuned at the art gate; z-order (bike under rider) is fixed in code. Sequencing (Bertrand): the BIKE layer is validated first (only the wheels turn, the whole bike visible in every frame); the RIDER layer follows once the bike passes the art gate. The rider is described POSITIVELY (art bible §3: never negate — never write 'without bike'). fps is tuned so the stamped spokes match the road speed: wheel ≈ 84px of the 256px cell ⇒ ~0.85 world units diameter (COURIER_H 2.6), so at COURIER_SPEED 7 u/s the wheel turns ~2.6 rev/s ≈ 940 deg/s; at the rider layer's 20-deg step that is ~47 frames/s, rounded to 48 (exactly 8 six-frame spoke cycles per second); the spare bike layer's 40-deg step would need ~24 fps if ever re-composited.

He is the chef of the BAC de nuit (PROJECT_GUIDELINES §7 roster extension), NOT a reskin of the CRS `enemy_riot`: distinct commanding silhouette (long knee-length overcoat, bare-headed plainclothes-BAC register per lead-art RULING 2026-07-20, reflective armband brassard + shoulder-clipped radio as the plainclothes authority tells, no helmet/visor/shield/armor), the ONLY uncovered head in an otherwise capped/helmeted roster, readable as 'chef' in <0.3s without colour. Four poses map the core QTE states: shielded (SHIELDED/protégé), exposed (EXPOSED phase-1 single-ring/opens fire), hit (touché), down (à terre/defeated). The differentiation-pack poses (weakpoint = phase-2+ two-ring clean-band frontal, parry_windup = charged/parry tell, finisher = kneeling still-trying coup-de-grâce) and the two Niveau-Final hall props (lustre, speaker_wall) are STRUCTURED below (ADR-0053 D6, ratified prompts from docs/art-direction/prompt-drafts/boss-commander.md, lead-art PROMPT GATE family PASS, 2026-07-20): keys/`asset` paths/pinned seeds landed; the two props each carry a per-type `size` override ([S13] — figures stay the block's square 256x256, `lustre` is portrait 320x512, `speaker_wall` is landscape 512x320, mirroring the `nearForegroundArt.types` per-kind-size precedent). ANCHOR SCHEMA GAP (flagged, not resolved here — needs senior-architect sign-off before render-integration): the tech plan names render-side anchors for 3 of the 5 new entries (`muzzle` semantics reused conceptually on `commander_weakpoint`'s VITAL/LIMB bands, `parryPoint` on `commander_parry_windup`). Rather than invent a new anchor schema unilaterally, no anchor field is added; per-entry $comment flags carry the requirement forward. These values can only be tuned against the real generated PNGs in any case (same as `enemies.*.muzzle`, measured post-generation by scripts/measure-muzzle-anchors.mjs), and generation has not been dispatched. `style` is copied VERBATIM from the live roster (enemies.style/hostages.style) for Family consistency (art-direction.md §2 law 2): the boss migrates to the gated pochoir direction IN LOCKSTEP with the whole roster when lead-art ships that migration (currently blocked on keying), never forked alone. Committed PNGs may be absent until generated in CI. lead-art PROMPT GATE required before any commit/generation.

trafficLight.prompt: a French road traffic signal on a slim round mast with a splayed foot, seen from the side at street level, the signal very tall and drawn large to fill the whole frame height. High on the mast a big tall boxy vehicle signal head turned in strict side profile: three round lenses stacked vertically, each tucked under a curved tunnel hood-visor that juts sideways toward the road, the lens discs seen edge-on as narrow dark slivers, all dead and unlit. Far below it, separated by a very long bare stretch of empty mast about twice as long as the short run of mast left between the pedestrian head and the ground, a smaller pedestrian signal head turned to face the viewer head-on: two blank dark round lens windows stacked vertically, both dead and unlit. Both heads cantilevered from the mast on short brackets. Every lens dark, matte and switched off, no glow and no colour; boxy hooded metal housings, dark uniform finish, a light grey highlight along the visor lips and mast edge to keep the housing legible against a dark night backdrop, with just enough empty magenta margin on the road side that the visor tip stays fully clear of the frame edge

bollard.prompt: a Parisian ball-top bollard: a short stout smooth tubular steel post about knee-to-hip height, slightly flared where it meets the ground, topped by a single rounded cast-iron ball cap; squat and low, much shorter than a street lamp, one smooth unbroken shaft, dark uniform painted finish with no reflective band and no collar, a subtle lighter grey highlight along the ball cap and the shaft's lit side

bench.prompt: a Parisian Davioud public bench seen from directly behind, the straight vertical backrest turned toward the viewer and filling the view, the seat hidden behind the backrest: three or four bold horizontal wooden slats forming the upright straight backrest, drawn flush against each other with only thin dividing outline strokes between them so they read as clear parallel horizontal lines with no open gaps or daylight visible between slats; a heavy ornate cast-iron end frame at each end with floral scrollwork legs, the scrollwork read as bold solid shapes rather than fine see-through openwork, visibly bulkier and heavier than the thin slats; the backrest standing straight and vertical, not curved or reclined, the whole bench resting directly on the pavement; a long low bench, much wider than it is tall, one continuous backrest with no armrest dividers, comfortably inset with empty magenta margin on both ends, no part touching the canvas edge

streetSign.prompt: a Parisian enamel street-name plaque mounted on a single thin post: a wide landscape rectangular flat plate, clearly wider than it is tall, bordered by a bold single raised keyline border running just inside the edge; across the centre of the plate the single word PARIS spelled out in bold clean black uppercase capital letters, large and clearly legible, this one word PARIS being the only readable text anywhere; sprayed across one corner of the plate an illegible looping graffiti tag, a tangle of curving spray-paint strokes forming no readable letters, kept clear of the plate edge; one slender post, much thinner than the plate, rising from below into the centre of the plate and planted on a small splayed foot on the pavement, the post attaching behind the plate with no visible gap or hole through it; a single flat plane, not a boxy double-sided sign

windowGrid.$comment: Where cops pop up, as a normalized grid over the facade image (0..1, y down). Tuned to the upper lit-window floors of the generated facades.

backdrop.$comment: Single-wide backdrop (ADR-0057, amends ADR-0048): the FULL décor — buildings, ground, sky — is baked into ONE opaque wide plane; no more separate sky/ground/foreground tiles and no tronçon tiling. file = basename under assets/levels/belliard/<file>.png; aspect = image width/height (native street-wide.png is 6418×1248), drives world width = world.heightUnits * aspect. Non-standard art pipeline (NOT the prompt-gate flow below, which is legacy/unused for belliard's backdrop): generated via scripts/gen-street-paid.mjs (paid ideogram-v4-quality) + scripts/stitch-belliard-street.mjs (mirror of ONE ideogram render against its own reflection — a seamless join, not a two-image butt-join); regenerate through THAT pipeline, not gen-level-art.mjs.

nearForeground.$comment: Near-foreground parallax props (ADR-0047), repositioned for the single-wide street-wide.png décor (ADR-0057) per docs/game-design/spec-belliard-street-wide-repositioning.md §2 (13 props, gate lead-game-designer PASS 2026-07-21). factor is NEGATIVE (scrolls opposite/faster than the camera); clamped to [-0.5,-0.1] in getNearForeground. x is a full-street normalized anchor (0=left,1=right). trafficLight (x=0.388, on the passage) is the ONLY prop exempt from the maxH clamp (TRAFFIC_LIGHT_H_FRAC, NearForeground.tsx) and thus the only one that can rise into the window band — deliberately placed over the passage exclusion zone so its mast never sweeps an active pop window; the other 12 props are clamped to maxH so non-occlusion holds by construction regardless of x.

windowGrid.$comment: Prior for scripts/gen-window-zones.mjs Pass 1 (single-facade only — belliard no longer takes that path, see backdrop.mode single-wide above; kept for the still-generated but now-unconsumed bare `belliard` fallback key in windowZones.generated.json). top recalibrated to 0.24 (was 0.19) to track the new Row A y_norm (spec §1.2, dev note §7) — the actual near-foreground maxH clamp is derived live from `windows` below (nearForegroundBandTop), not from this field, but it is kept in sync for data hygiene.

windows.$comment: Single-wide décor (ADR-0057): 3 rows recalibrated on street-wide.png's real openings, per docs/game-design/spec-belliard-street-wide-repositioning.md §1 (gate lead-game-designer PASS 2026-07-21) — A lucarnes (mansard dormers) y=0.24, B étage noble (balcony doors) y=0.35, C persiennes (shuttered windows, densest) y=0.47. x/y normalized over the WHOLE single image (not per-tile as before). Exclusion zones respected column-by-column: passage 0.372-0.408, couture (mitoyen seam) 0.485-0.502, recess 0.595-0.610 (a second, undocumented building-seam/recessed-gable column found by direct pixel inspection of street-wide.png during the enemy-recalibration pass — a narrow near-solid dark vertical band measured consistently ~lum<52 across y=0.20-0.51 at x≈0.597-0.608, the mirror-image counterpart of the `passage` seam; this was the exact cause of a cop rendering on bare roof next to a chimney with no grille, since the old row-A x=0.62 landed inside it), pignon (blind gable) 0.788-0.812, edges <0.035/>0.965. 2026-07-21 targeted fix (6/54 zones, verified per-zone against real street-wide.png pixels, not re-derived wholesale): row A xs[7] 0.62→0.643 (was inside the new `recess` zone, no dormer there — real dormer sits at 0.643), xs[9] 0.835→0.847 (was on a chimney stack, real dormer at 0.847), xs[11] 0.95→0.96 (was mostly off the roof skylight, nudged onto it); row C xs[6] 0.257→0.238 (was in the gap between two real windows), xs[18] 0.746→0.753 (was half on the wall beside the window), xs[22] 0.928→0.947 (was in the gap between two real windows). All other x/y values verified already correct against the real image and left untouched.

levels.label: L'Éden, ancien dancing, 31 décembre 1999
levels.$comment: Niveau Final — l'Éden (ancien dancing), the boss-QTE venue (ADR-0053, story-boss-niveau-final-live). Single-facade mode (default, no `backdrop` field), same as stalingrad/vitry. INTERIOR venue: unlike the street levels this facade is a static hall interior held behind the whole boss tableau, so the exterior `sky`/`street` layers are DELIBERATELY DROPPED from `prompts` below (lead-art PROMPT GATE family PASS, 2026-07-20 — 'layer set with sky/street DROPPED for the interior') — the facade alone fills the frame ceiling-to-floor, which is exactly what satisfies the 'no dead sky-gap behind the boss {0,-5}' composition constraint. `gen-level-art.mjs` skips a layer cleanly when a level's `prompts` doesn't declare it, rather than sending FLUX a broken 'undefined' prompt (no hardcoded sky/street text ever reaches the generator for this level). `foreground`/`facade` prompt strings are copied VERBATIM from the gated draft `docs/art-direction/prompt-drafts/niveau-final-eden.md` (lead-art FAMILY PASS — Maud/concept-artist owns the prompt strings, this block's structure/ids/paths/sizes/windowGrid is dev-tooling-assets'). `size` uses the shared global `sizes.facade`/`sizes.foreground` (1280x768), no per-level override needed. A separate optional `ceiling` layer was drafted (bare-hook plaster detail) but is NOT included here per the draft's own default ('by default this layer drops' — the facade already carries the ceiling/cornice register); add it only if a future structural need requires a dedicated upper slot. Path `assets/levels/niveau-final/facade.png` (narrative wiring flag B, ADR-0023) generated via the existing `gen-level-art.mjs` → CI pipeline (ADR-0010), same as every other level — no new script/workflow needed for the backdrop itself.

windowGrid.$comment: cols RETUNED 5→4 (Bertrand escalation decision + lead-game-designer express DESIGN GATE PASS, 2026-07-21, docs/handoffs/story-boss-niveau-final-live.md — supersedes the original gated [E3] count of 5). The batch-2 l'Éden facade generated a 3-wall perspective room whose back wall carries 4 clear evenly-spaced frontal arches (not the gated 5 — a recurring generation drift, not a config bug); Bertrand accepted the art at 4 and ordered the grid retuned to match rather than a third reroll (the 2-batch cap was spent). Karim's gate confirmed the [E3] INTENT (even spacing + occupiable window-cop slots + [E5] merge-risk mitigation) is preserved at 4, and that [E5] risk actually IMPROVES (wider piers between fewer arches). rows=1 (a single row of arches, not multi-floor like the street levels) — computeWindowSlots/getWindowZones both special-case rows===1 to ny=0.5, so top/bottom are set equal and are inert by construction, kept for readability/consistency with the other per-level windowGrid blocks. NOTE (flagged, not fixed here — out of dev-tooling-assets' structural lane): the `facade` prompt string below still reads 'exactly 5 tall arched windows' — a residual mismatch against the now-4-pinned grid and the already-accepted 4-arch art; if `facade.png` is ever deleted and regenerated, the stale '5' text would reroll toward the wrong count again. Prompt-string content is concept-artist's (Maud's) lane, not touched here; routed to lead-art/concept-artist for a conscious amendment.
